charlie_customer: Hey @ben_support — our prod calls to /v1/complete started returning 401 invalid_api_key right after the config roll yesterday. curl from my laptop succeeds but our CI rollout jobs fail.

ben_support: Can you paste the exact curl you used (redact the key) and the response body from the failing CI job? Also which cluster/org?

charlie_customer: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete -d '{}'
CI log shows: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"invalid_api_key"}
We run on k8s, secret is written into the pod at /etc/secrets/REDWOOD_KEY by our CI (GitHub Actions). Org: charlie-inc.

ben_support: Thanks. Can you cat the file from the pod (cat -v to reveal invisible chars) and also run a hex dump? e.g. `kubectl exec -it pod -- cat -v /etc/secrets/REDWOOD_KEY`

charlie_customer: cat -v shows: sk_test_AbcDeFg===$
Hex dump (xxd) prints: 73 6b 5f 74 65 73 74 5f 41 62 63 44 65 46 67 3d 3d 3d 0a

alice_infra: That 3d 3d 3d ("===") followed by 0a is suspicious. Some mail/encoding tools insert soft line breaks using '=' in quoted-printable (QP) encoding. If a pipeline step mime-encodes the value, it can end lines with '=' which then get preserved when written verbatim. QP uses '=' at EOL as a soft-break marker.

ben_support: If the secret file contains a soft-break or extra '=' inserted by QP, the service will see a different key. Quick test: decode with Python's quopri module inside the pod: 
```
python -c 'import quopri,sys;print(quopri.decodestring(open("/etc/secrets/REDWOOD_KEY","rb").read()))'
```

charlie_customer: Ran that in the pod, output (repr) is: b'sk_test_AbcDeFg==\n' — decoding removes the extra soft-break and yields the correct key. When I `export RW_KEY=$(python -c "import quopri,sys;print(quopri.decodestring(open('/etc/secrets/REDWOOD_KEY','rb').read()).decode())")` and curl with $RW_KEY it returns 200.

ben_support: Great — so root cause: CI pipeline step (an older terraform/secret template module we still use) appears to be passing the secret through a MIME/quoted-printable encoder when preparing artifacts. The value ends up with QP soft breaks that then get written into the file as literal '=' followed by newline bytes. Server treats that as a different key -> 401.

alice_infra: Workaround: update the CI step to base64-encode the secret and decode in the container on start, or run `quopri -d` before writing the value. We'll also patch the terraform module to stop QP-wrapping secrets. I'll open an infra ticket.

ben_support: I'll escalate and attach our reproduce steps & suggested mitigations. For immediate relief: apply the `quopri` decode trick in your workflow or mount a Kubernetes secret from a different store that doesn't re-encode.

ingest-bot: Alert: 401 invalid_api_key spike detected for org:charlie-inc — 180 errors in last 5m.

ops-oncall: Noted, watching. @alice_infra please link the INF ticket here so we can correlate if other orgs are affected.

alice_infra: Filed INF-2042: "quoted-printable soft-break inserted into API key secret (CI artifact)" and added charlie-inc as impacted. Plan: (1) immediate doc with workaround, (2) patch module to stop QP encoding, (3) roll forward tests. ETA: patch rolling tomorrow morning.

charlie_customer: Applied temporary CI patch to run `python -c 'import quopri,sys;print(quopri.decodestring(open("/tmp/secret.qp","rb").read()).decode())' > /etc/secrets/REDWOOD_KEY` before creating the image — now requests return 200. Will monitor. Thanks for the fast triage :thumbsup:

ben_support: Thanks for confirming. I'll close the support ticket after infra posts the remediation PR. Leaving notes: repro steps, xxd output, quopri decode worked, INF-2042 linked.

charlie_customer: Happy to help with postmortem details if you need logs or CI workflow snippets.

ben_support: Appreciate it — adding a short blameless postmortem to the ticket. Closing thread when PR merges.
